title: Shepherds, Humility, and Standing Firm
overview: Peter closes his letter by asking church leaders to care for people gently, asking everyone to be humble and to trust God with their worries, and promising that their suffering will not last.

parts.label: Leaders as shepherds (vv. 1-4)
parts.note: Peter speaks to the church leaders, called elders, as one of them and as someone who saw Jesus suffer. He asks them to care for people like shepherds, willingly and not for money or control, and promises that Jesus, the head shepherd, will give them a prize that never wilts, unlike the leaf wreaths given to winning athletes.

parts.label: Humility and handing over worry (vv. 5-7)
parts.note: Younger members should respect the leaders, and everyone should put on humility toward each other like a servant's apron, because, as Proverbs says, God resists the proud and is generous to the humble. Bowing low under God's strong hand goes together with handing him every worry, trusting that he cares and will lift them up when the time is right.

parts.label: The prowling lion (vv. 8-9)
parts.note: The devil, a name meaning accuser or slanderer, is called their adversary, a word for an opponent in a lawsuit, and is pictured as a hungry lion circling for prey, likely meaning the pressures and fears that could pull these believers away from their faith. They are to stay clear-headed and hold their ground, knowing believers in other places are going through the same hardship.

parts.label: God will restore (vv. 10-11)
parts.note: Peter promises that after a short time of suffering, God himself will repair them and set them on solid ground. He ends this thought with a brief burst of praise.

parts.label: Final greetings (vv. 12-14)
parts.note: Silas, also called Silvanus, helped with the letter, perhaps by writing it down or by carrying it, and scholars are unsure which. 'Babylon' is most likely a code name for Rome, 'she' probably means the church there, Mark is likely the Mark known from the book of Acts and called a son as a close follower, and the kiss was a family greeting showing they belonged to one another.

disagreement: Christians differ on what kind of leadership the opening verses describe, with some traditions seeing ordained church offices like bishops and others seeing simply local leaders who serve without a special rank.
think: When you are carrying a heavy worry, what would it take for you to actually set some of it down, and what or whom would you trust with it?
